title: The hidden cost of selling too soon

 The hidden cost of selling too soon
Hi Sara,
Here’s a hot take from a deal attorney: Selling your firm is not always the smartest financial move. At least not right away.
Say your firm brings in $1 million topline and you net $400,000 a year.
You get an offer to sell for $1 million.
That is ~2.5 years of income.
It’s tempting.

But it’s also worth asking…could you just keep working and earn the same money?
The answer is yes.
But here’s the catch
Most people don’t stop after 2.5 years.
They keep going.
Then they do the math again later, and again after that.
Suddenly, 20 years have gone by, and they still don’t have an exit plan.
Eventually, the real question becomes:

How much longer do you want to be doing this?
When you sell, it’s not just about price
It is about timing.
It is about freedom.
It is about getting out before you’re burned out.
So if you're thinking about selling, take a minute to run the numbers honestly. Then decide what kind of exit is actually worth it.

To better exits,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
